caption:
No, you don't need 20% down to buy in Ontario.

Under the federal rules, the minimum down payment is 5% of the first $500,000 of the price plus 10% of the portion from $500,000 to $1.5 million. At $1.5 million or more, 20% is required. With less than 20% down you need mortgage default insurance, which is not available on homes priced at $1 million or more. Source: Government of Canada (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada), minimum down payment rules, as of October 2026. Eligibility and lender rules apply. General information only, not legal, tax or mortgage advice.

A buyer asked me: what's a home inspection condition?

1) It's a clause in your offer that gives you a set window to inspect. 2) An inspector goes through the home and writes a report. 3) If issues come up, you might renegotiate or walk away, depending on the wording. 4) Remove the condition and the deal becomes firm, so ask your lawyer first.

Save this for before you make an offer. General information only, not legal, tax or mortgage advice.
